newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Akzo seen supported by coatings growth. [CORRECTED 13:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Akzo seen supported by coatings growth. [CORRECTED 13:20 GMT]

text.p: Better results in coatings and pharmaceuticals will underpin third-quarter results at Dutch chemical group Akzo Nobel, analysts said on Monday.
Akzo Nobel is seen posting third-quarter net profits on Wednesday of 298 to 364 million guilders, with consensus at 336.3 million. This compares with 1995 third-quarter net of 324 million guilders.
Analysts said the second-quarter earnings upturn at Akzo Nobel's coatings division -- good for around a third of group sales -- would likely continue, aided by lower raw material prices.

"Coatings will show the biggest growth," said Peter Beijers, analyst with Kempen & Co (corrects name of securities house from "NIB Strating"). The division was first in line to benefit from the underlying synergy advantages accruing from the merger of Akzo with Nobel in 1994, he said.
"Lower raw material prices will also lend a helping hand," he added.
"Prices for titanium dioxide (an important raw material for paints) have fallen by some five to 10 percent," agreed Robert Jan Stassen, chemicals analyst with Bangert, Pontier & Partners.
Both analysts also predicted a slight increase in operating profits at Akzo's pharmaceuticals division.
Fears over the contraceptive pill, which impacted sharply on year-earlier sales, have waned although sales have still not recovered in Germany and the United Kingdom.
But Akzo is expected to book extra costs to cover the launch of its new anti-depressant Remiron and fertility drug Puregon.
Akzo's troubled fibre activities, pressured by cheap imports from outside Europe and a generally sluggish market, would likely do no more than break even, analysts warned.
"I expect a nil result, even worse than in the second quarter," said Beijers.

Stassen was slightly more optimistic. "I think we will see a consolidation of the second quarter result at operating level," he said, adding fibre results would remain poor until restructuring was completed in 1998.
The firm's chemical division, good for some 35 percent of sales, would post a stable to slightly lower year-on-year operating result due to poor performance in bulk chemicals.

PVC prices and margins are at record lows, but this would be partly offset by an upturn in specialty chemicals and the negative impact on last year's third-quarter result of the flooding of Akzo's U.S. Retsof salt mine.
Lien van der Leij, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000.
